item.title: What will Houston Texans do at NFL trade deadline? Decision is more complex than it seems.
item.description: Texans general manager Nick Caserio faces a consequential decision at next Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle) It happens every year. The NFL's trade deadline comes around and teams are forced to confront a major question at the midpoint of their season. Do they sacrifice the future for immediate help in hopes of competing for a Super Bowl? Do they start over and sell off assets as they plan for the future? Or do they stay put? That's where the Houston Texans sit one week before the Nov. 10 trade deadline as general manager Nick Caserio confronts those questions. Since coach DeMeco Ryans arrived nearly four years ago, Caserio and the Texans have taken a measured approach to the trade deadline. They haven't quite been buyers and they definitely haven't been sellers. They've mostly stayed quiet during this crucial part of the season, though it hasn't always been for a lack of trying. Last season, the Texans called the Jets about running back Breece Hall , but felt the asking price - a third-round pick - was too high. This year will more than likely be more of the same. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The Texans are 2-5 heading into their Week 9 game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. There are certainly areas the Texans could upgrade that could help improve their chance at making the playoffs. But their five losses in seven games make it a complex decision. The Texans aren't quite bad enough this year to start selling assets, but they also aren't good enough to become buyers, either. Three more losses would almost surely knock them out of the playoffs. Two losses would put them on the brink. And the more losses the Texans have, the more valuable their draft picks will become. Caserio said at his off-week press conference that they would be open to a deal - whatever that may look like. "If it makes sense, great," Caserio said. "If not, so… we've had conversations. We've talked to most of the league here." TEXANS AT CHARGERS When: 3:05 p.m. Sunday Where: SoFi Stadium; Inglewood, Calif. TV: CBS Radio: 95.7 FM, 610 AM, 101.1 FM (Spanish) Caserio already made a major move last month when he traded a second-round pick and a seventh for Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick, which was significant draft capital Houston relinquished. The Texans' current 2027 picks include a first-, a third-, a fourth-, two sixths and a seventh-round pick. "I don't think anybody's really worried about the draft right now," Caserio said when asked about the second-round pick. "There are a lot of ways that you can recoup picks at some point along the way, whether it's this year or whether it's in the offseason. item.description: Dan Campbell; Jack Campbell Credit: Bryan M. Bennett/Getty; Michael Owens/Getty NEED TO KNOW Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said linebacker Jack Campbell is “improving” after he suffered a serious neck injury on Nov. 1 “It’s not easy because he’s always going to be on our minds over here,” Dan said on 97.1 The Ticket Jack has remained hospitalized since the collision Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided an update on linebacker Jack Campbell’s condition after the Pro Bowler suffered a serious neck injury on Sunday, Nov. 1. During an interview with 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Nov. 3, the Lions head coach said Jack, 26, is “improving” as he remains hospitalized. The team confirmed that the former first-round pick sustained a neck injury in the second half of the Lions’ 19-15 home win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. “It’s not easy because he’s always going to be on our minds over here,” Dan, 50, told the radio show, adding, “The good news is he is improving.” Dan Campbell; Jack Campbell on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 Credit: Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty; Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Dan said “knowing he’s doing better,” in reference to Jack, and keeping the other Lions players informed on the positive updates “helps everybody just get a better handle on this.” The head coach added, “All we can do at this point is just continue to pray for Jack, put our thoughts on him when we have a minute, and on his family — and it’s working, like I said, because he’s improving.” Dan asked for continued prayers for Jack. “Please continue to do that. We’ll leave it at that, so continue to pray for him. But it is positive,” he told 97.1. Jack sustained the neck injury when his head collided with Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson’s hip when he went to make a tackle in the fourth quarter. Jack landed face-first on the turf at Ford Field and remained motionless for several moments. item.title: Braves Lock In Acuña And Albies At Shocking Bargain Prices
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The biggest shock in Atlanta sports news isn’t a trade or a star leaving town. It is how little money the Atlanta Braves will pay their two best players next year. The team exercised their options for Ronald Acuña Jr and Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season, locking them in for a combined total of just $24 million. That figure is shockingly low for two players who have carried the franchise for a decade. Most fans expected a massive price tag for the 2023 NL MVP and the long-time second baseman. Instead, the club secured Acuña for $17 million and Albies for $7 million. This move was the “no-brainer decision of all no-brainer decisions” after the team won 94 games and claimed the NL East title, according to Battery Power . The organization also cleared the books by reinstating four pitchers from the injured list, including Spencer Strider and Hurston Waldrep, just as the postseason kicked off. The Price Tag Defies Logic It is rare to see a team keep its core stars for such a low cost in modern baseball. Acuña is set to make $6 million less than the standard MLB qualifying offer, which is a massive win for the front office. Some fans thought Acuña would not return, but those rumors ignored the reality of the contract signed years ago. The deal allows Atlanta to keep the player who achieved the historic 40-home run, 70-stolen base season in 2023. Ozzie Albies brings a similar value with his $7 million price tag for the upcoming year. While he had a career low in wRC+ this season, the team views him as a bridge for younger prospects waiting in Double-A. Replacing him would likely cause more trouble than simply keeping him on the roster for one more year. The financial flexibility this creates is huge for the rest of the roster. With $24 million committed to two All-Stars, the team has room to address other needs like shortstop. The Braves are looking at trade options such as Jeremy Peña from the Astros, as their current plans with Ha-Seong Kim did not work out. This budget allows them to be aggressive in the market while keeping their stars. Health Remains the Only Wild Card The only question left for both players is their physical status heading into next season. Acuña tore his ACL in 2024 but returned in 2025, proving he can still dominate when healthy. When he is not healthy, people hear about it constantly, but the team is betting on his recovery. The same logic applies to Albies, whose value skyrockets when he is on the field and playing his usual style. Reinstating the pitching staff shows the team is ready to move forward with a full squad. Neither Spencer Schwellenbach nor Spencer Strider should be anticipated to immediately resume their previous performance levels. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. item.title: Dortmund's Kovač has great respect for Betis 'gentleman' Pellegrini
item.description: Borussia Dortmund's Coach Niko Kovač gives instructions from the sidelines during the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Dortmund's Kovač has great respect for Betis 'gentleman' Pellegrini») Tom Weller/dpa Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovač is looking forward to facing his 73-year-old rival Manuel Pellegrini in Wednesday's Champions League home game against Real Betis. "He is not only a great coach due to his huge experience, his enormous wealth of experience, but because I also see him as a gentleman," Kovač told a news conference on Tuesday. He was particularly enthusiastic about the Chilean's style of coaching. "I think the way he coaches, the way he conducts himself on the touchline, shows me that this man is a calm character. So really, very, very pleasant," Kovač added. "Still standing on the touchline at 73, that's quite something. I look forward to meeting him in person tomorrow." According to the Dortmund boss, whose side battled to a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Saturday, Pellegrini's teams stand out above all for their quality on the ball. "He is South American, he knows exactly what his teams need. They have to play football, and they do play football," said the former Croatia boss. "That is not only the case at Betis now, but also at Malaga, and it was the case at (Manchester) City too. That is why tomorrow we face an opponent who is very secure on the ball, an opponent who will surely try to make us run." Betis have won all three league phase games this term, while Dortmund have two wins and a loss.

item.title: Nikita Zadorov Fined Maximum $5,000 For Punch On Alex Vlasic
item.description: James Guillory-Imagn Images The Chicago Blackhawks lost a hard-fought overtime battle in Boston, but Fans will focus on the heavy fine imposed on their opponent.. Nikita Zadorov, the big defenseman for the Bruins, received the maximum allowable penalty of $5,000 from the league. This ruling comes after a chaotic scrap late in the game where Zadorov threw a punch at Alex Vlasic while the Blackhawks player was already on the ice. The NHL Department of Player Safety made its decision clear on Sunday., citing the $5,000 amount as the cap for such offenses under the current rules. Boston.com reported that the fine was issued specifically for the roughing incident involving Vlasic during the 5-4 overtime loss at TD Garden. The league does not hand out these max fines lightly, signaling that the league office views the action as a serious breach of player safety protocols. The Brawl That Sparked the Fine A hard hit by Casey Mittelstadt sparked the trouble during the closing minutes of the second period. Vlasic took exception to the contact and chased the Bruins forward into the neutral zone, leading to a full-scale fight. According to Boston.com, Vlasic jumped Mittelstadt and brought him down, causing all the skaters from both teams to join the fray. It was a messy scene that quickly escalated beyond a standard hockey scrap. While the players were tangled up, Zadorov intervened in a way that cost him money. He delivered a punch to Vlasic while the Blackhawks defenseman was still down on the ice after Zadorov dragged him away from Mittelstadt. This specific act of striking a player who was not in a position to defend himself drew the league’s ire. The Times of India noted that Zadorov received this maximum fine for punching the Chicago star while he was already down. Game Penalties and Ice Time The on-ice officials were quick to react to the violence. Roughing led to Zadorov receiving a double-minor penalty alongside a 10-minute game misconduct. These calls effectively ended his night in the lineup. According to Boston.com, Zadorov saw limited action in the third period once his misconduct ended, taking only two shifts that amounted to one minute of ice time during the final five minutes of regulation. The Bruins managed to survive the chaos and win the game in overtime, but the disciplinary fallout remains a key talking point. The incident highlights how quickly a physical game can turn into a disciplinary hearing. For Blackhawks fans, seeing Vlasic take a cheap shot while down is frustrating, but the league’s swift $5,000 penalty shows they are watching the hits closely. While Zadorov plays for Boston, the incident is a reminder of the physical nature of the division. The Blackhawks are still learning how to handle these high-intensity moments against tough opponents.

item.title: Behind the Shades: My story and unexpected journey into a Bills Mafia docuseries
item.description: When I started traveling around the country following the Buffalo Bills, I never imagined it would lead to being featured in a documentary. Yet, here we are. On October 21, Just One Before I Die , a five-part docuseries about Bills Mafia, premiered on Tubi. The series follows some of the most recognizable personalities in Bills Mafia, exploring their traditions, their dedication, and the relationships that make this fan base so unique. And somehow, I ended up being one of them. Not because I jump through tables, wear an elaborate costume, or cover myself in ketchup and mustard. Apparently, attending an unreasonable number of consecutive Buffalo Bills games was enough to get someone’s attention. How Did I Get Myself Into This? People often ask me how this whole consecutive-game streak started. Was it something I planned? Was I trying to break a record? Not even close. It really started in 2017, when I decided to get my season tickets back. My friend Adrian eventually began encouraging me to travel to more away games. At the time, I struggled with the idea of attending games in opposing stadiums. Mentally, I just wasn’t prepared for it. I couldn’t handle the heckling, and I definitely wasn’t comfortable sitting alone. By 2018, I had attended almost every home game and finally added a couple of away games. In 2019, I started traveling even more. Then came 2020. COVID hit, stadiums were empty, and suddenly the thing I’d grown to love was gone. I was absolutely CRAVING a football game and couldn’t wait until fans were allowed back in the stands for the playoffs. That’s when I realized I might have a problem. By 2021, my son was heading off to college, and I figured, why not try attending an entire season? Just one season. How hard could it be? Kenny “Pinto Ron” Johnson actually warned me. “Don’t do it. It gets addicting.” Naturally, I respectfully ignored him. Turns out he was right. Don’t tell him I said that. Somewhere along the way, I’d become addicted. Not just to watching the Bills play live, but to everything that came with it. The traveling, the tailgating, the friendships created, the adventures, and the excitement of experiencing a different city every week. I still don’t enjoy the heckling, but I’ve definitely developed thicker skin. And these days, I often find myself sitting alone without giving it a second thought. Looking back, I missed three random games in the 2019 season, or my streak would actually be quite a bit longer.
